homonyms_same_issuer.note: the within-issuer homonym base rate among Form 3/4/5 filers: 1 of 721 8-K rows with an anchor has two owner CIKs sharing surname + given name at the issuer

reused_identifiers.note: 8-K carries no identifier of its own; this is the Form 3/4/5 anchor side, i.e. research 17 F4's stratum seen from the 8-K

transitive_bridges.note: a bridge needs a third key value between two others. None exists, for the same structural reason research 17 F5 gives: an exact-equality key makes 'shares a key with' an equivalence relation.

pooled_with_research_17.note: research 21 relabelled research 17's own 281 8-K pairs with the same rules (verified identical at the draft stage) and then labelled 657 more from the same population. The pooled figure IS the census figure; nothing is added twice.

sensitivity_to_pass_2.reading: the conservative reading clears 99% at 97.5% only because of pass 2. The `settled` reading clears either way (pass 1 alone: LCB97.5 0.99387 on n = 623).

coverage.note: one pair per (issuer, 8-K name) in the X stratum and one per (issuer, fl key) group in K, so a pair is close to one distinct person; the Wilson bound still assumes independence it cannot fully have.

iapd.reason: IAPD's individual endpoint is a strict lookup by CRD/OwnerID (research 16 F2). 8-K Item 5.02 persons carry no CRD, so there is no key to look them up by, and every label here was settled from SEC-sourced data already on disk. `21-iapd-requests.jsonl` is present and empty: zero requests, zero 403s, zero 429s.
